svg.text: A Chain, One Fork, Two Strands
The piece runs as one chain of escalating evidence for a single claim — bugs come from computational
irreducibility — broken once by a genuine fork (can this particular case be proven bug-free, yes or no?) and
ending in two parallel strands (math's own bugs, and practical ways to hold bugs back) that meet in a final…

g.text: Overview
Down the page: the claim, its demonstration in toy machines, a real fork (provable or not?), the irreducibility this
reveals, and two parallel consequences meeting in one closing thought.
OVERVIEW

g.title: Bugs come from irreducibility — even the simplest programs have it — The computational process a program actually runs can be far more sophisticated than the simple mental picture we have of what it should do. — → spya-sx0zyh
g.text: Bugs come from irreducibility
even the simplest programs have it

g.title: Tiny Turing machines built for n+1 glitch — bugs appear after many correct steps — A 3-state machine that looks like it computes n+1 suddenly outputs 9 instead of 8 at n=7. — → spya-s7uc4u
g.text: Tiny Turing machines built for n+1 glitch
bugs appear after many correct steps

g.title: Whether it's a bug depends on the spec — behavior, equivalence, or a forbidden outcome — Judging a program buggy needs some independent statement of what it should do — and machines can escape almost any such statement. — → spya-gjut02
g.text: Whether it's a bug depends on the spec
behavior, equivalence, or a forbidden outcome

g.title: Cellular automata built to double input glitch too — same pattern, a different kind of machine — A rule that correctly doubles its input for many steps suddenly fails, for instance at n=14. — → spya-cy4dgs
g.text: Cellular automata built to double input
glitch too
same pattern, a different kind of machine

g.title: Provable bug-free? — For some specific rule or machine, can you actually show in advance that it will never misbehave? — → spya-gt6430
g.text: Provable bug-free?

g.title: Yes — simple enough, or reduces to a known rule — e.g. the interior obeys rule 122 — Even a visually complex pattern can be proven to always stabilize once its interior dynamics are identified. — → spya-gagsuk
g.text: Yes — simple enough, or reduces
to a known rule
e.g. the interior obeys rule 122

g.title: No — no proof turns up, a real bug lurks — same effort as just running it — Searching the space of possible proofs forever fails for a buggy machine, because the claim is simply false. — → spya-ypka68
g.text: No — no proof turns up, a real
bug lurks
same effort as just running it

g.title: Only running the program reveals what it does — computational irreducibility, laid bare — Because irreducibility is ubiquitous, no bounded amount of analysis can rule out every surprise. — → spya-wcnws7
g.text: Only running the program reveals what it does
computational irreducibility, laid bare

g.title: Testing alone can't be trusted — rare bugs hide from even massive sampling — Scientific induction from repeated tests works only where reducible regularities exist; raw computation has no such guarantee. — → spya-yc9e2z
g.text: Testing alone can't be trusted
rare bugs hide from even massive sampling

g.title: Ruliology keeps turning up dramatic surprises — rule 30, a 137-million-step halt, and more — Exploring the space of simple programs, startling exceptions to apparent regularities show up again and again, sometimes only after exhaustive search. — → spya-kjsjh5
g.text: Ruliology keeps turning up dramatic surprises
rule 30, a 137-million-step halt, and more

g.title: Mathematics has its own rare counterexamples — a trend reverses at the 23-billionth prime — Conjectures can hold for enormous numbers of tested cases, then suddenly fail far out. — → spya-bhwh4d
g.text: Mathematics has its own rare counterexamples
a trend reverses at the 23-billionth prime

g.title: Good language design & visualization help — but never erase the risk entirely — Primitives that match human intent, and seeing a computation's whole pattern, are the best practical defenses — not a cure. — → spya-kdks69
g.text: Good language design & visualization help
but never erase the risk entirely

g.title: Bug to an engineer, discovery to a scientist — An unexpected result is a failure if you wanted reliability, but exactly the kind of thing ruliology is built to find. — → spya-xdwm97
g.text: Bug to an engineer, discovery to a
scientist
yes
no
Turing machines and their proofs
A straight chain in close-up: simple Turing machines develop bugs at specific, often startlingly delayed inputs, and a
formal proof can only ever be built for the ones that turn out to be truly bug-free.
INSIDE-TM-BUGS

g.title: A seeming n+1 machine glitches at n=7 — outputs 9 instead of 8 — → spya-h3jx6h
g.text: A seeming n+1 machine glitches at n=7
outputs 9 instead of 8

g.title: Glitches recur whenever n = 8k−1 — binary ending in 111 triggers extra 'scribbling' — → spya-z99x4e
g.text: Glitches recur whenever n = 8k−1
binary ending in 111 triggers extra 'scribbling'

g.title: Thousands of machines compute n+1 correctly — but first bugs still show up eventually — → spya-rhc6t0
g.text: Thousands of machines compute n+1 correctly
but first bugs still show up eventually

g.title: One machine is flawless through n=14 — then fails at n=15, giving 20 not 16 — → spya-pt0hmz
g.text: One machine is flawless through n=14
then fails at n=15, giving 20 not 16

g.title: Bigger machines hide bugs even longer — a 4-state machine first fails at n=63 — → spya-hqukdz
g.text: Bigger machines hide bugs even longer
a 4-state machine first fails at n=63

g.title: Being 'buggy' depends on the spec chosen — judge by behavior, equivalence, or a forbidden outcome — → spya-gjut02
g.text: Being 'buggy' depends on the spec chosen
judge by behavior, equivalence, or a forbidden outcome

g.title: Two seemingly identical machines diverge — they first disagree at n=27 — → spya-txuteu
g.text: Two seemingly identical machines diverge
they first disagree at n=27

g.title: A correct machine's behavior gets proved — symbolic axioms plus mathematical induction — → spya-q8fg9q
g.text: A correct machine's behavior gets proved
symbolic axioms plus mathematical induction

g.title: A buggy machine yields no proof, ever — the search finds nothing, because the claim is false — → spya-ypka68
g.text: A buggy machine yields no proof, ever
the search finds nothing, because the claim is false
Ruliology's surprises, and beyond
The tail of the chain opened up: ruliology keeps finding dramatic last-minute surprises, then splits into two things
that are simply both true at once — math has its own rare counterexamples, and practical fixes exist — before
converging on one closing thought.
INSIDE-RULIOLOGY-BEYOND

g.title: Rule 30 erupts into sudden complexity — among cellular automata that mostly look tame — → spya-zbsh70
g.text: Rule 30 erupts into sudden complexity
among cellular automata that mostly look tame

g.title: Math conjectures can break after huge success — a factoring pattern fails at x^105 − 1 — → spya-y7q6q3

g.title: Pure math mostly dodges this — by sticking to human-graspable, reducible questions — → spya-zcpn8u

g.title: Good language design heads off many bugs — primitives that already match human intent — → spya-kdks69

g.title: Trained AI systems stay especially exposed — their learned mechanisms resist human understanding — → spya-sggbeh
